https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.verbose:
Agenda and board packet for the Troy School District Board of Education Special Meeting held Tuesday, June 18, 2019, at 8:00 a.m. in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098.

The sole business item was consideration of a High School 1:1 Program (iPad purchases). The recommended resolution stated: "Be it therefore resolved that the district purchase iPads and cases from Apple Computers in the amount of $367,500.00 and that these amounts be approved as an expenditure of the 2016 Capital Projects Fund." Pricing was obtained from the REMC bid.

A memorandum dated June 14, 2019, from Beth Soggs, Director of Technology (Technology Services, 4420 Livernois, phone 248.823.5060), to Rick West, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services, details the implementation. A pilot 1:1 program was conducted during the first semester of the 2018-19 school year with 10th and 11th grade students and 12 teachers at Athens and Troy High Schools; informational surveys gathered input from pilot teachers, non-pilot teachers, students, and parents, and student work was reviewed for evidence supporting the district's "blue pillar" goals. The recommendation was to phase in the 1:1 iPad program beginning with 9th grade students and teachers at the start of 2019-20, allowing time to evaluate a full-year implementation, focus professional learning on a smaller group of teachers, and let students continue from their 8th-grade iPads with the addition of a keyboard. The recommended plan provided iPads for all 9th graders in 2019-20 with a spring 2020 program evaluation; if positive, the district would continue phasing in iPads with each incoming 9th grade class, and if negative, the purchased iPads would be used to refresh 3rd grade iPads the following year as planned. The purchase from Apple Computers, using REMC bid pricing for 1,050 iPads with keyboard cases, totaled $367,500 and had to be made prior to June 21, 2019 to receive the special pricing; after that date the cost for 1,050 devices would increase to $412,650.

A supporting rationale document, "TSD 1:1 High School Digital Learning Environment," dated May 7, 2019 and submitted by Jennifer Gottlieb and Beth Soggs, cites Fullan, Quinn, and McEachen on leveraging digital learning and notes that Troy already has an established 1:1 iPad program in grades 3-8. It argues a high school 1:1 environment would let students deepen learning, connect and collaborate locally and globally, receive timely feedback, and lighten backpacks since many textbooks provide electronic access. The document states that bond money had been set aside to support the initiative, describes the process of engaging all high school teachers, and reports results reviewed by the Teaching and Learning Cabinet.

Agenda and supporting candidate materials for a special meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education held February 18, 2020 at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building at 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098.

The central purpose was Board Candidate Selection. Due to the resignation of Mrs. Paula Fleming on January 21, 2020, the Board was required to appoint an individual to serve as a board member through the end of Fleming's term, which ends December 31, 2020. The Board president was to accept nominations from board members to fill the vacancy, with the rule that individual members may not nominate more than one candidate. The process document laid out nomination forms, calls for votes on first, second, and (if necessary) third nominees by roll call, and a final appointment resolution reading: Be It Therefore Resolved that [name] be appointed to fill the vacancy on the Board of Education for the term expiring December 31, 2020. Roll-call voting lists rotated the order among board members Hammond, Hauff, Philippart, Schmidt, Wilson, and Gottlieb; four votes are required for election.

Eight candidates were presented with materials: (A) Emina Alic; (B) Vital Anne; (C) Tim Burns; (D) Russell Reynolds; (E) Tony Sarna; (F) Srinivas Simhan; (G) Barrington Wilkins; and (H) Lisa Zheng. Each candidate submitted a 2020 Troy School Board Appointed Trustee Candidate Questionnaire. Vital Anne's questionnaire responses are included in the extracted text: she stated she is 49 years old, has lived in Troy for 16 years with her husband Siva, has been married 26 years, and has two daughters aged 20 and 16. She holds a bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering from Andhra University in India (1991) and a master's (MS) in Biomechanics from Purdue University in Indianapolis. She began her career as a Project Engineer at Altair in Troy and had worked there for 25 years across roles including project engineer on CAE (Computer Aided Engineering) projects (structural, crashworthiness, and occupant safety analysis for automotive, aerospace, medical device, and consumer goods clients) and project manager, and was at the time the Vice-President of Software Integrity and Testing, managing a global team. Her husband Siva has worked in IT for 20 years; both are originally from India, moved to the US in the early 1990s, and became American citizens.

The agenda also included a Closed Session for Consideration of Negotiations. Vital Anne was subsequently the appointee, as reflected in her introduction as newly appointed trustee at the February 25, 2020 regular meeting.
